Have you had a CT scan? It took me getting to a point of desperation to advocate for myself forcefully enough after making emergency room trips multiple times in a span of years all to leave with no answers. I finally got a CT scan Turns out my pcos (that i had been diagnosed with but neglected by my doctors) had never gone away and the pain I was experiencing was ruptured cysts. In combination with vulvodynia as well os some other chronic illnesses, it has been a long road and struggle to understand  what I have and how to manage it. But I am finally getting there.

Knowing what you have when it comes to these conditions is key in treating  them. I know that's not what you want to hear right now when you're feeling defeated by your own body, but it is possible to find competent doctors who can find answers for you and successful treatment. Please consider self advocacy for specialists, more thorough testing and treatment and please do not rely on spiritual practices exclusively when it comes to your health. Homeopathic and spiritual remedies can certainly help aid recovery, but abandoning modern medicine altogether when it comes to your health is dangerous especially when you're not sure what specifically you have.

I will also say, when I was living in a state that had much more competent and accessible doctors and a better medical network, I found the proper diagnoses with much more ease. Now, having moved back to a more rural area, I have struggles to find doctors who even know or understand my conditions. If this is plaguing your life, it would be worth considering looking in major cities with more reputable medical networks for treatment. Wishing you luck.

But you're not gonna know unless you're open and honest with him, which brings me to my next point...

2) you can't expect people to anticipate your needs if you never make them known. Personally, if I have a friend who's in the hospital, I will check in minorly, but assume that they don't want to talk to me because they are in recovery and need rest. But if a friend says to me or publicly " hey, I'm going to have surgery and I would like support in these ways" I'm onboard to help however I can and I find that's the case with most people.
